observations.attempt: Focus item 2 continued: assessed whether the new 2-lane mechanism creates a starvation/DoS-adjacent path today, and whether it would if a future caller starts using it.
evidence: No current caller can select the 'priority' lane (see ING-04 evidence) -- there is no starvation path an external or unprivileged caller can trigger TODAY.

Independently verified BullMQ 5.28.2's own scheduling code in this repo's installed node_modules (not just trusted from changes.md/spec.md's claim): node_modules/bullmq/dist/cjs/classes/scripts.js:145 `else if (opts.priority)` routes to addPrioritizedJob, else addStandardJob; node_modules/bullmq/dist/esm/commands/moveToActive-11.lua:70,82 confirms RPOPLPUSH(wait->active) is tried first and moveJobFromPriorityToActive only runs when that returns no job -- both lanes mapping to a non-zero priority (1 and 2) is the correct, deliberate fix for the inverted-priority bug the module header describes, not an unexamined design choice.

Design note (not a current exploit, not blocking): unlike the SQS side's consume_enrichment(priority_weight=3) which bounds starvation of the default lane by round-robin weighting, BullMQ's ZPOPMIN-by-priority-then-FIFO ordering has no such built-in bound -- if a future policy change assigns real traffic to the 'priority' lane, a sustained flood of priority-lane jobs could starve the default lane indefinitely. spec.md's Open Questions #3 already defers the 'which jobs get priority' policy decision to a separate, later ticket; recording this as a forward-looking design consideration for that follow-up, per this stage's Limitations section below.
